outlook: Soybeans traded higher Thursday after USDA's weekly export sales came in strong at 2.84 million metric tons for the week ending October 15, near the top of trade expectations; November soybeans were up about 8 cents at midday. Corn slipped a few cents even though export sales of 1.53 million tons beat expectations, as harvest pressure and a large crop weighed on prices. Wheat extended its losses, with December Chicago down about 5 cents and Minneapolis December spring wheat down 6½ cents, after weak wheat export sales of about 240,000 tons and talk of renewed Russia-Ukraine talks that could reduce the Black Sea risk premium. Brazil's soybean planting was 26% complete, slightly ahead of last year.
